title: CTW SMS MUSIC TEST (VRUN CTW's sound test as a Master System ROM)
description: The music test spinoff of VRUN CTW on the Master System (project vrun-ctw-sms), modelled on CTW NES's AudioPlayer: the game's real sound driver (VRUN's NES music engine translated by fab2c, nes_apu.c's PSG mapping), the song list (all 11 game tracks) and one FL TEST slot, nothing else. It IS the game's own Options > Sound Test (engine/audio/player_ui.fab) as the whole ROM: musictest/build-musictest.ps1 copies the VRUN tree, adds the FL TEST track (musictest/mt_tree.py: a placeholder padded to 1280 bytes a channel, VRUN's bend + duty decoders), and builds it with the game's own build.ps1 -Define CTW_MUSICTEST (the pad's music test controls in src/nes_shim.c). The game build is not changed by it. An .flp song goes into the FL TEST slot with BrokenDev/tools/music/flp/musictest/build-ctw-sms-mt.ps1 (FruityHost musictest-ctwsms: CtwSmsBackend's Build + Patch).

toolchain: SDCC 4.6.0 and devkitSMS 533ae57, pinned in toolchains.json (the game's build.ps1 rebuilds SMSlib and crt0 from devkitSMS's sources)
Python 3 (VRUN's engine/audio/build_music.py + gen_music_decoders.py, imported by musictest/mt_tree.py)

steps.name: build
steps.note: musictest/build-musictest.ps1: the VRUN tree copied to build/musictest/vrun, mt_tree.py, the game's build.ps1 -FabRoot -Define CTW_MUSICTEST; writes vrun_ctw_sms_mt.sms + vrun_ctw_sms_mt.txt (the FL TEST slot's manifest, CtwSmsBackend's bn2-flp-ctwsms v3 format + loopframes).

run.note: Boots through the game's title to the MUSIC TEST screen (about frame 100). Pad: Up / Down choose a song, 2 play it from the start, Pause pause / resume, Left / Right pick a channel (SQ1 SQ2 TRI NOI = PSG tone 1, tone 2, tone 3, noise), 1 mute / unmute it, 1 held + 2 solo it (again: all on), 2 held + 1 stop. Songs loop. List 12 = FL TEST (the placeholder, or an .flp's song: build-ctw-sms-mt.ps1).

scenarios.why: the ROM boots to the music test, Down + button 2 plays the second song

knownIssues: The title screen shows for a moment at power-on (the boot is the game's own; the music test starts from it).
The help lines' button names are the Master System pad's (2, 1, Pause); the screen is otherwise the game's Sound Test (ON / OFF per channel: a solo shows as one ON).
